result:
If I could reshape the world with a single, sweeping change, I’d eliminate the systemic barriers that keep people from accessing the education they need to thrive—anything from crippling tuition costs and underfunded schools to the digital divides that separate rural and low‑income communities from reliable internet.  

Imagine a world where every child, no matter where they’re born or how much money their family has, can walk into a well‑resourced learning environment, tap into a global library of knowledge, and develop the critical thinking, creativity, and emotional intelligence needed for the challenges of the future.  

By making high‑quality, lifelong education truly universal—free at the point of use, adaptable to diverse learning styles, and powered by technology that’s accessible to all—we’d not only lift individuals out of poverty, but also foster a more informed, empathetic, and innovative society. That, in my view, would set off a cascade of positive effects: better health outcomes, more equitable economies, stronger democratic participation, and a richer culture of collaboration across borders. One lever, endless ripples.
